classification.description: Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium)

origin_result.basis: Final manufacture in the UAE passed by exporter declaration. Manufacturing operations pass minimal operations requirements. CTSH check passed with all 3 non-originating inputs classified outside subheading 761010. Value addition passed with a build-down calculation of 49.0% against the 45% threshold on an FOB basis (total 6 inputs, 3 non-originating, representing 51% of price).

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered through its Factory Registration service prior to applying for a certificate of origin, requiring the factory to be outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and have a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added, which takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority requires the application to include the HS code, description, quantity, and value of the exported product, and may apply risk management such as requesting detailed cost sheets and conducting a factory visit.

The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service where the applicant logs into the portal, selects the service, fills in the form, uploads proof of factory registration and commercial invoice, pays online, and receives processing in about one working day.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for the invoice value band up to AED 100000.

The competent authority must issue the certificate of origin prior to, at, or within five (5) working days of the date of exportation, bearing an authorised signature and official seal, valid for twelve (12) months from issue for a single import.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020 including the origin criterion claimed, must keep supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing, and must answer customs inquiries within 10 working days; electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit (unconfirmed).
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the year of the date of issue.

caveats.note: No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are based on the exporter's own declaration.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
